selection_rules: Danish analysis: Danish citizens (citizenship observed in the Danish register)

Danish analysis: 18 years or older in a given year
Danish analysis treatment group: not cohabiting or married with a partner in Denmark in a given year
Danish analysis main control group: cohabiting or married with a non-EU citizen in a given year in Denmark

Swedish analysis: both sponsors and partners arrive between 1995 and 2009 and are 18 or above at immigration
Swedish analysis: non-EU couples where neither partner arrives from Denmark are dropped

sample.period: 1995-2009 (Danish and Swedish analysis samples); Swedish onward-migration spells followed until 2014

construction_notes: EM_it is set to one if individual i emigrates to Sweden in a given year t and zero if the person stays in Denmark; in Denmark it is compulsory to report out-migration when leaving the country for more than six months.

Treat_it equals one if individual i belongs to the treatment group in year t and zero for individuals in the control group in t; the interaction coefficients gamma_t are normalised on t = 2001, Treat = 0.

IM_t is the half-yearly number of treated (affected) individuals immigrating to Sweden; the ITSA is run at a half-year frequency with the reform placed in the first half of 2002 because the policy was announced in January 2002.
Table A.1 columns 1-3 add a constant and dummy variables for year, age, female and children; columns 4-6 additionally add dummies for six education levels, labor force participation and unemployment.
Danish citizens with immigrant background are defined as born abroad or born in Denmark to parents who were both born abroad and hold no Danish citizenship.
In the Swedish data citizenship is not observed, so citizenship is proxied by country of birth and country of arrival.
Individuals who do not need residence permits are recorded with missing information on the permit variable in the Swedish data.
Fig. 4 and Fig. 9 plot municipality-level averages; Fig. 4 panel a covers 1995-2001 and panel b 2003-2009, excluding the 2002 reform year.
Survival in Fig. 15 is defined as being in Sweden in 2014 or the year before death, whichever comes first, measured by years since immigration.
Table 1 reports averages over the sample period 1995-2009 for 317,534 treatment-group and 191,377 control-group person-years.

claims.statement: The 2002 Danish family reunification reform raised the probability that an affected (single) Danish citizen with immigrant background emigrated to Sweden by 1.26 percentage points in 2003, relative to 2001 and relative to Danish citizens with immigrant background who were cohabiting or married with a non-EU partner.

treatment.label: Treat_it x Y_t: being in the group affected by the 2002 Danish family reunification reform in year t

register_source.value: Danish full population register data (Statistics Denmark), 1995-2009: citizenship, country of birth, parents' country of birth and citizenship, and the spouse/cohabitant link used to classify partnership status. No DST register code is named in the paper.

definition.value: Treat_it is an indicator set to one if individual i belongs to the treatment group in year t and zero for individuals in the control group in t; the treatment group are Danish citizens with immigrant background, older than 18, not cohabiting or married with a partner in a given year in Denmark, who after the 2002 reform face the 24-year rule, the attachment requirement, housing/financial requirements and a bank collateral when reuniting with a non-EU partner. The control group are Danish citizens with immigrant background, older than 18 years, cohabiting or married with a non-EU citizen in a given year in Denmark. The estimated quantity is the coefficient gamma_t on the interaction of Treat_it with the year-t dummy, relative to the omitted year 2001.

timing.value: Treatment status is measured in each calendar year 1995-2009; the reform was announced in January 2002, passed in June 2002 and the interaction coefficients are measured by calendar year relative to the omitted year 2001.

outcome.label: EM_it: emigration from Denmark to Sweden in year t

definition.value: EM_it is set to one if an individual i emigrates to Sweden in a given year t and set to zero if a person stays in Denmark; emigration is observed because in Denmark it is compulsory to report out-migration when leaving the country for more than six months.
